1.word_for_word: द्वि-चत्वारिंशके कुब्जोन् नमनं धनुषो भिदा — In the two-fourths, the hunchbacks bowed and the bow broke; वधस् तद् रक्षिणां कंसा- रिष्टं रङ्गोत्सवादि च — The killing of that guards, Kansa- rishta, and the theatrical festival; अङ्ग-विलेपाश् चन्दनादयः । — Body ointments, such as sandalwood.; गृहीतान्य् अङ्ग-विलेपानां भाजनानि यया ताम् । — She took the vessels for her body and ointments.; रस-प्रदः सुख-प्रदः ॥१॥ — It gives taste and pleasure.
1.translation: In the two-fourths, the hunchbacks bowed and the bow broke The killing of that guards, Kansa- rishta, and the theatrical festival Body ointments, such as sandalwood. She took the vessels for her body and ointments. It gives taste and pleasure.

2.word_for_word: हे अङ्गने हे वरोरु, इति सोपहासं सम्बोध्यापृच्छति, त्वं का, एतद् अनुलेपनं कस्य वा, उ ह इति निपातौ भ्रूवि-क्षेप-युक्ते वितर्के । — O courtyard, O beautiful thighs, he addresses her with a laugh and asks, “Who are you, and whose is this ointment?”; अस्मत् सेवा सद्यः फलत्य् एवेत्य् आह---न चिराद् इति ॥२॥ — Our service will bear fruit immediately, he argues, and not long.
2.translation: O courtyard, O beautiful thighs, he addresses her with a laugh and asks, “Who are you, and whose is this ointment?” Our service will bear fruit immediately, he argues, and not long.

3.word_for_word: तिस्रो ग्रीवोरःकट्यो वक्रा इति त्रिवक्रेति नाम यस्याः सा । — The three necks, chest and waist are curved, and she is called Trivakra.; अनुलेप-साधन-क्रियायां कंसस्य बहुमता दास्य् अस्मि ॥३॥ — I shall give Kaṁsa the majority in the act of ointment-means.
3.translation: The three necks, chest and waist are curved, and she is called Trivakra. I shall give Kaṁsa the majority in the act of ointment-means.

4.word_for_word: रूपं चाङ्ग-सौष्ठवं पेशलं च सौकुमार्यं माधुर्य च रसिकता हसितं चालापाश् च वीक्षितं च तैर् धर्षितात्मा मोहित-चित्ता । — The beauty of the body, the beauty of the body, the professionalism, the tenderness, the sweetness, the charm, the laughter, the movements, and the looks on them made me assaulted and bewildered.; सान्द्रं घनम् ॥४॥ — concentrated cloud.
4.translation: The beauty of the body, the beauty of the body, the professionalism, the tenderness, the sweetness, the charm, the laughter, the movements, and the looks on them made me assaulted and bewildered. concentrated cloud.

5.word_for_word: स्व-वर्णेतर-शोभिना राम-कृष्णयोर् वर्णाभ्याम् इतरः पीतादि-वर्णस् तेन शोभितुं शीलं यस्य तेन । — He who has the characteristics of being adorned with yellow and other colors other than the colors of Rāma and Kṛṣṇa; संप्राप्त-पर-भागेन संप्राप्तः परो नाभेर् उपरितनो भागो येन सः । — The upper part of the navel which is reached by the other part of the navel; संप्रप्तः पर-भागः शोभातिशयो येनेति वा, तेनानुरञ्जितौ ॥५॥ — They were delighted by the excess of beauty which had attained the other's share.
5.translation: He who has the characteristics of being adorned with yellow and other colors other than the colors of Rāma and Kṛṣṇa The upper part of the navel which is reached by the other part of the navel They were delighted by the excess of beauty which had attained the other's share.

6.word_for_word: स्व-दर्शने सद्यः फलं दर्शयन् । — Showing the fruit immediately in his own vision.
6.translation: Showing the fruit immediately in his own vision.

7.word_for_word: तस्याः प्रपदे पादाग्र-द्वयं पद्भ्याम् आपीड्य द्वे अङ्गुल्याव् उत्ताने उन्नते यस्मिन् पाणौ तेन चिबुके मुखस्याधो-भागे धृत्वाध्यात्मं देहम् उन्नमयाम् आस ॥७॥ — He pressed the tips of her feet with his feet, raised his two fingers, and with the hands in which he raised his chin he held the lower part of his face and raised his spiritual body.
7.translation: He pressed the tips of her feet with his feet, raised his two fingers, and with the hands in which he raised his chin he held the lower part of his face and raised his spiritual body.

8.word_for_word: तदैव ऋजु समानम् अङ्गं यस्याः । — That’s when she has a straight, equal body.; बृहत्यौ श्रोणी पयोधरौ च यस्याः । — She had large hips and breasts.; सा । — She.; मुकुन्द-स्पर्शनाद् इति मुख्यं कारणम् ॥८॥ — This is the main reason for the touch of Mukunda.
8.translation: That’s when she has a straight, equal body. She had large hips and breasts. She. This is the main reason for the touch of Mukunda.

12.word_for_word: आधि-विकर्शनं मनः-पीडा-शमनम् । — It is a remedy for the pain of the mind.; कंस-वधेन स्वयं साधितोऽर्थः सुहृदां प्रयोजनं येन सः । — By killing Kaṁsa he himself accomplished the purpose of his friends; अगृहाणाम् अकृत-दाराणां पान्थानां प्रवासिनां परम् आयनम् आश्रयस् त्वम् ॥१२॥ — Thou art the supreme refuge of the homeless, the unmarried, the travelers on the road.
12.translation: It is a remedy for the pain of the mind. By killing Kaṁsa he himself accomplished the purpose of his friends Thou art the supreme refuge of the homeless, the unmarried, the travelers on the road.

13.word_for_word: मधुरया गिरा तां प्रस्थाप्य व्रजन् वणिक्-पथैर् वणिग्भिर् अर्चितः ॥१३॥ — Having sent her away with sweet words he proceeded along the paths of merchants worshiped by the merchants
13.translation: Having sent her away with sweet words he proceeded along the paths of merchants worshiped by the merchants

14.word_for_word: लेख्याश् चित्र-न्यस्ता इव मूर्तयो यासां ताः ॥१४॥ — They are to be written as if they were painted in pictures and their idols.
14.translation: They are to be written as if they were painted in pictures and their idols.

15.word_for_word: धनुर् मख-शालां पृच्छन् ॥१५॥ — The bow asked the sacrificial hall.
15.translation: The bow asked the sacrificial hall.

17.word_for_word: निमिषेणाति-शीघ्रम् । — In a blink of an eye, very quickly.; मद-करी मत्त-हस्ती ॥१७.१८॥ — Mada-kari matta-hasti ॥17.18॥
17.translation: In a blink of an eye, very quickly. Mada-kari matta-hasti ॥17.18॥

19.word_for_word: गृह्यतां बध्यताम् इति वदन्तो जिघृक्षव आवृतवन्तः ॥१९॥ — They covered him who wanted to kill him shouting 'Grab him and tie him up'
19.translation: They covered him who wanted to kill him shouting 'Grab him and tie him up'

20.word_for_word: न केवलं क्रुद्धौ, किन्तु भग्नस्य धनुषः शकले गृहीत्वा जघ्नतुश् चेति ॥२०॥ — Not only were they angry, but they grabbed the broken bow and struck it down.
20.translation: Not only were they angry, but they grabbed the broken bow and struck it down.

21.word_for_word: परतः प्रातर् गन्तव्यम् इति शाला-मुखाद् एव पुनर् निष्क्रम्य ॥२१॥ — Then he went out again from the entrance of the shed thinking that he should leave in the morning
21.translation: Then he went out again from the entrance of the shed thinking that he should leave in the morning

22.word_for_word: तेजः प्रभावम् । — Teja is the effect.; प्रागल्भ्यं धृष्टताम् ॥२२॥ — arrogance and arrogance.
22.translation: Teja is the effect. arrogance and arrogance.

23.word_for_word: शकटं शकटावमोचन-स्थानम् ॥२३॥ — The cart is the place where the cart is unloaded.
23.translation: The cart is the place where the cart is unloaded.

24.word_for_word: मुकुन्दस्य विगमे व्रजान् निर्गमन-समये या आशिष आशासत---सुखं प्रभाता रजनीयम् [भा।पु। — The blessing which Mukunda hoped for at the time of his departure from Vraja---happiness in the morning and night [Bh.p.; १०.३९.२३], अद्य ध्रुवं तत्र दृशौ भविष्यते [भा।पु। — 10.39.23], today surely there will be a scene [Bh.p.; १०.३९.२५] इत्य्-आदि यद् उक्तवत्यस् ता ऋताः सत्या बभुवुः । — 10.39.25] They became true to what they had said.; पुरुष-भूषणस्य श्री-कृष्णस्य गात्रस्य देहस्य लक्ष्मीं शोभाम् । — The beauty of the body of Lord Kṛṣṇa, the ornament of men, is the opulence of the body.; कथं-भूतस्य गात्रस्य ? — How-about the body of the ghost?; न अहो इतरान् ब्रह्मादीन् हित्वा यद् अयनम् आश्रयं श्रीः कामयामास । — Alas, it is not that the goddess of fortune desired to take refuge in the moon, leaving behind others, such as Brahmā.; यां गात्र-लक्ष्मीम् इति वा॥२४॥ — or that which is the body-laxmi.
24.translation: The blessing which Mukunda hoped for at the time of his departure from Vraja---happiness in the morning and night [Bh.p. 10.39.23], today surely there will be a scene [Bh.p. 10.39.25] They became true to what they had said. The beauty of the body of Lord Kṛṣṇa, the ornament of men, is the opulence of the body. How-about the body of the ghost? Alas, it is not that the goddess of fortune desired to take refuge in the moon, leaving behind others, such as Brahmā. or that which is the body-laxmi.

25.word_for_word: अवनिक्तं क्षालितम् अङ्घ्रि-युगलं ययोस् तौ । — Their feet were washed and washed down.; क्षीर-मिश्रम् अन्नं भुक्त्वा सुखं न्यवसताम् ॥२५॥ — They lived happily after eating food mixed with milk
25.translation: Their feet were washed and washed down. They lived happily after eating food mixed with milk

26.word_for_word: परं केवलं गोविन्द-रामयोर् विक्रीडितं तत्, न तु पराक्रमः कश्चित् ॥२६॥ — But it was only a pastime of Govinda and Rama, and nothing of prowess.
26.translation: But it was only a pastime of Govinda and Rama, and nothing of prowess.

27.word_for_word: उभयथा स्वप्न-जागरित-भेदेन प्रत्येकं मृत्योर् दौत्य-कराणि च । — In both cases, there is a difference between dream and wakefulness, and each is the messenger of death.; तथा च मन्त्रः, "इत्थादुलूकश् चापघ्नन् हिरण्याक्षो अयो-मुखः । — Similarly, the mantra says, "Itthadulukash chapaghanan hiranyaksha ayo-mukhah.; रक्षसां दूत आगतः" इत्य्-आदिः । — The messenger of the demons has come," etc.; तथा, "यद् एतद् भूतान्य् अन्वाविश्य दैवीं वाचं वदसि" इत्य्-आदिश् च ॥२७॥ — and, "That which, having searched for these beings, speaks the divine Word," and so on.
27.translation: In both cases, there is a difference between dream and wakefulness, and each is the messenger of death. Similarly, the mantra says, "Itthadulukash chapaghanan hiranyaksha ayo-mukhah. The messenger of the demons has come," etc. and, "That which, having searched for these beings, speaks the divine Word," and so on.

28.word_for_word: तानि दर्शयति श्लोक-त्रयेण । — He shows them in three verses.; जलादौ प्रतिरूपे दृश्यमानेऽपि स्व-शिरसस् तत्रादर्शनम्। — Even when seen in the form of water and other things, the self-head is not seen there.; असत्य् अपि द्वितीये चक्षुषोऽन्तर्-धानेऽङ्गुल्य्-आदौ ज्योतिषां चन्द्रादीनां द्वित्वम् ॥२८॥ — Even in the second untruth the duality of the moon and other luminaries in the innermost part of the eye is at the beginning of the finger.
28.translation: He shows them in three verses. Even when seen in the form of water and other things, the self-head is not seen there. Even in the second untruth the duality of the moon and other luminaries in the innermost part of the eye is at the beginning of the finger.

29.word_for_word: छायायां प्रतिबिम्बे छिद्र-प्रतीतिः । — The perception of a hole in an image in a shadow.; पिहित-कर्ण-पुटस्य योऽन्तः श्रूयमाणो ध्वनिः स प्राण-घोषस् तस्याश्रवणम् । — The sound heard inside the closed earlobe is the sound of life; वृक्षेषु स्वर्ण-वर्ण-प्रतीतिः । — The perception of golden color in trees.; रजः-कर्दमादिषु स्व-पदानाम् अदर्शनम् । — The absence of one’s own feet in the dust and mud.; एतानि जागरितानि दुर्निमित्तानि ॥२९॥ — These are the evil causes of awakening.
29.translation: The perception of a hole in an image in a shadow. The sound heard inside the closed earlobe is the sound of life The perception of golden color in trees. The absence of one’s own feet in the dust and mud. These are the evil causes of awakening.

30.word_for_word: स्वप्नान्य् आह---स्वप्न इति । — He argues that dreams are dreams.; प्रेतैर् मृतैः परिष्वङ्गः खरम् आरुह्य यानम् । — The ghosts embraced the dead and mounted the donkey in the carriage.; विष-भक्षणम् । — Poison-eating.; नलद-माली जपा-कुसुम-माली यायाद् इति यत् तद् अप्य् एकं दुर्निमित्तम् इति ॥३०.३१॥ — That which is said that Nalada-mali should go to Japa-kusuma-mali is also a bad cause.
30.translation: He argues that dreams are dreams. The ghosts embraced the dead and mounted the donkey in the carriage. Poison-eating. That which is said that Nalada-mali should go to Japa-kusuma-mali is also a bad cause.

32.word_for_word: कष्टेन कथञ्चित् प्रभातायां पुनः सूर्ये चाद्भ्यः समुत्थित इति । — With difficulty, he somehow got up from the water in the morning and again in the sun.; तथा च श्रुतिः, "अद्भ्यो वा" इति, "य उदगान् महतोऽर्णवट् विभ्राजमानः सलिलस्य मध्यात् । — Similarly, the scripture says, "Or from the waters," "He who rises from the midst of the waters, shining like a great ocean.; स मा वृषभो लोहिताक्षः सूर्यो विपश्चिन् मनसा पुनातु" इति च ॥३२॥ — May that bull with red eyes, the sun, the wise, purify me with my mind.
32.translation: With difficulty, he somehow got up from the water in the morning and again in the sun. Similarly, the scripture says, "Or from the waters," "He who rises from the midst of the waters, shining like a great ocean. May that bull with red eyes, the sun, the wise, purify me with my mind.

34.word_for_word: यथोपजोषं यथा-सुखम् ॥३४.३५॥ — as the pleasure, as the pleasure.
34.translation: as the pleasure, as the pleasure.

36.word_for_word: मल्ल-ताल उत्तर उपरि उच्चैः श्रूयते येषु तेषु तूर्येषु । — The wrestling rhythm is heard loudly over the north on those trumpets.; उपाध्याया मल्लाचार्याः ॥३६॥ — They are the teachers and the wrestlers.
36.translation: The wrestling rhythm is heard loudly over the north on those trumpets. They are the teachers and the wrestlers.

37.word_for_word: उपस्थानं मल्ल-रङ्गम् ॥३७॥ — The approach is the wrestling arena.
37.translation: The approach is the wrestling arena.

38.word_for_word: समाहुताः समाहूताः । — They are summoned and summoned.; निवेदितान्य् उपायनानि यैस् ते ॥३८॥ — They offered gifts to you.
38.translation: They are summoned and summoned. They offered gifts to you.
